import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 34

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/34](https://www.erdosproblems.com/34)
- [Er77c] Erdős, Paul, *Problems and results on combinatorial number theory. III*. Number theory day
  (Proc. Conf., Rockefeller Univ., New York, 1976) (1977), 43-72.
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [He86] Hegyvári, N., *On consecutive sums in sequences*. Acta Math. Hungar. (1986),
  193--200.
- [Ko15] Konieczny, J., *On consecutive sums in permutations*. arXiv:1504.07156 (2015).
-/

namespace Erdos34

open scoped BigOperators

/-- The set of consecutive sums of a permutation `p` of `{1,…,n}`, where position `k` holds the
value `p k + 1`: the sums `∑_{u ≤ k ≤ v} (p k + 1)`. -/
def consecutiveSums (n : ℕ) (p : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : Finset ℕ :=
  (Finset.univ.filter (fun x : Fin n × Fin n => x.1 ≤ x.2)).image
    (fun x => ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc x.1 x.2, ((p k : ℕ) + 1))

/--
For any permutation $\pi\in S_n$ of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ let $S(\pi)$ count the number of distinct consecutive sums, that is, sums of the shape $\sum_{u\leq i\leq v}\pi(i)$. Is it true that
$$
S(\pi) = o(n^2)
$$
for all $\pi\in S_n$?

Hegyvári [He86] gave a counterexample.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11,
  formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos34.lean"]
theorem erdos_34 : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c → ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ N, ∀ p : Equiv.Perm (Fin n),
      ((consecutiveSums n p).card : ℝ) < c * (n : ℝ) ^ 2 := by
  sorry

end Erdos34

reformulations.difference: The uniform little-o assertion is written using strict inequalities and natural-number thresholds, whereas Konieczny's Question 1 uses |S(a)| ≤ ε n² for positive integers n.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A strict bound implies the corresponding weak bound, and its threshold can be increased to max N 1. Conversely, apply the source's weak bound with ε = c/2 and take the threshold at least 1; then |S(a)| ≤ (c/2)n² < c n². Thus permitting n = 0 has no effect on the eventual assertion. Negating either equivalent assertion gives the same negative answer. The equivalence was proved as strict_iff_source in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without using the admitted problem theorem.

review.notes: Both declarations are faithful. The definition uses ordinary, nonempty consecutive intervals, shifts values to 1,…,n before summing, and deduplicates sums correctly. Exhaustive Lean computations for all 154 permutations with n ≤ 5 agree with an independent list-based implementation; boundary and membership checks also passed. The source records DISPROVED (LEAN), matching the category and answer. The cited proof's definitions match definitionally; after two tactic-only compatibility adjustments for the newer sandbox toolchain, it proves the exact reviewed statement with only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. The full Er77c and He86 texts were inaccessible, but the mathematical claim and Hegyvári attribution are explicit in the accessible cited sources. All experiments are in /workspace/review; the reviewed file is unchanged.
